mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of expected corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% and remains >1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below the prior month's level indicates weakening labor market strength, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month's PAYEMS for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market softening
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or non-negative in 80% of similar labor weakening episodes (empirical threshold).

mechanism_narrative: When the Housing Starts index (HOUST) rises by more than 5% in the following month, it signals accelerating building activity and robust consumer confidence, driving a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% from current month to next month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during such HOUST spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) of at least 3% suggests supply-side softness, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate demand recovery.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return during such supply declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure that prompts the Fed to hold rates steady, causing a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive or non-negative during such CPI surprises (empirical frequency < 30%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for two consecutive months, despite strong labor demand proxies, signals tight labor markets and supports a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative or flat in 70% of similar labor tightness episodes (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer demand (GDPC1) and industrial demand (RSAFS) above their 12-month averages for the next month predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to broad economic optimism.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12mo avg AND RSAFS > 12mo avg for next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) when both proxies exceed their averages.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 60-day forward return as discounting effects on equity valuations diminish.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative or flat during such periods in 80% of historical episodes.
